slides.headline: First, how the business works today.

artwork.alt: Day 1 path: Functions next, then KFFM, Purpose, Values, BHAG and 3HAG.

notes: Day 1 has six steps. We start with the work: who owns each function, then how the work turns into cash.

slides.title: What functions does the business need?
slides.headline: What functions does the business need?
notes: Each leader lists the functions the business needs. Use the following example as a starting point. Agree on functions that describe the current business. Do not start with reporting lines or individual job titles.
slides.support: List the work the company must perform to operate successfully.

artwork.alt: Mock of the Function Chart. Functions down the left: Head of Company, Marketing, Sales, Operations, Development, Finance, People. Each team member, Pat, Chris, Andrew, Jen and Allison, posts on their own colored sticky who holds each function. Most agree. Development and People show different answers and gaps. A green column on the right records the one agreed owner for each function.

slides.title: Start with the work, not the people.
slides.headline: Start with the work, not the people.
notes: A traditional chart starts with people and titles. A Function Chart starts with the work, then names who owns it.
Use the source example excerpt. The same person may appear in more than one role.
This view shows people and reporting positions. The next view makes functions explicit.
Show the same example with the function first and accountable person second.
Shannon owns both Head of Company and Sales in the historical example. This makes load visible.

artwork.alt: Left: a traditional hierarchy of people and job titles. Right: the same organization as a Function Chart. It starts with Head of company, Marketing, Sales and Finance, then names their owners.

slides.title: Give every function one accountable owner.
slides.headline: Give every function one accountable owner.
notes: Restate the rule: one accountable owner for each function. Others can contribute.

At the Kick Off: have leaders list every required function. Include support functions, not only the cash-producing flow. Agree on one accountable owner for each function. Capture current reality before resolving gaps.
slides.support: One person is **accountable** for the work. Others may be **responsible** to contribute to the work.

slides.title: Where is ownership unclear?
slides.headline: Where is ownership unclear?
notes: In private mode, each person writes who holds each function. Reveal, then agree. Add any missing functions. Resolve differences about current accountability. At the Kick Off, do not design the future organization here. At a quarterly, add any planned functions in the next step.

panels.heading: No owner?
panels.support: Name the person who will own it.
